title: Puss in Boots.
lines: Once upon a time there was a miller with three sons.
When the miller was very old, he gave his things to his sons.
The eldest got the mill.
The second got the donkey.
And the youngest, whose name was Peter, got only the cat.
Peter was sad.
What am I supposed to do with a cat?
But then the cat began to talk!
Don't be sad, master.
Give me a bag and a pair of boots, and I'll make you rich.
Peter was so surprised that he did it.
He bought a pair of beautiful red boots for the cat.
And the cat put them on and walked proudly through the village.
Tip, tap, tip, tap.
Everyone called him Puss in Boots.
The cat was very clever.
He caught a fat rabbit in the forest, and he took it to the king.
Your Majesty, said the cat with a deep bow, this is a present from my master, the Marquis of Carabas.
That was really Peter, of course, but the cat had made up a grand name.
The king was pleased.
Every week the cat brought a new present.
A rabbit, two partridges, a basket of fish.
And the king wondered: Who is this rich marquis?
One day the cat heard that the king would be driving along the river with his daughter, the princess.
Quick, master, said the cat.
Go and swim in the river.
Peter jumped into the water.
When the king's coach came by, the cat shouted: Help!
Help!
The marquis's clothes have been stolen!
The king immediately sent for the finest clothes, and Peter was allowed to ride in the coach.
The princess thought he was very nice.
Meanwhile the cat ran ahead, to a big castle.
A giant lived there who could do magic.
I've heard that you can turn into any animal, said the cat.
Even a lion?
Of course!
boomed the giant, and he turned into a big roaring lion.
Grrraaaow!
The cat got a fright, but he stayed clever.
Wow!
But something very small, like a mouse, I bet you can't do that.
Yes I can!
said the giant.
And pop!
He turned into a little mouse.
Then the cat pounced, and the mouse ran away so fast that it never came back.
When the coach arrived at the castle, the cat was standing at the gate.
Welcome to the castle of the Marquis of Carabas!
The king was impressed.
Peter and the princess became the best of friends, and later they got married.
And the cat?
He got a plate of fish every day and was allowed to keep his boots on forever.
